canonical_statement: Using the convention c^(t*lambda)_(t*mu,t*nu), produce three nonempty integer partitions lambda, mu and nu in canonical weakly decreasing positive-part form such that |lambda| = |mu| + |nu|, every partition has length at most 7 and sum of parts at most 30, and the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^(t*lambda)_(t*mu,t*nu) has a negative monomial-basis coefficient. The complete polynomial is encoded constant coefficient first as reduced rational pairs. The frozen primary source gives degree P <= binomial(length(lambda)+1,2) <= 28, so the candidate also supplies P(1),...,P(29), which uniquely determine the full polynomial without evaluating at the zero-partition convention.
success_criterion: The content-pinned amf.stretched-lr.exact.v1 dispatcher accepts the strict candidate after its direct LR-tableau/Newton implementation and its mathematically independent Jacobi-Trudi--Pieri/Vandermonde implementation agree on all 29 exact LR values, the complete reduced rational polynomial, and at least one negative coefficient; separate open-status and novelty review remains mandatory at promotion and submission time.
partial_progress_criterion: Independently reproducible exclusion of a new frozen parameter range beyond the known all-lengths-at-most-4 theorem, exact structural pruning of candidate families, or verified performance improvements that preserve both mathematical paths are retained as research progress but do not satisfy this counterexample target.
stop_conditions: The canonical prompt, its length/sum bounds, or the open status changes and the frozen bounded target no longer represents the intended problem.
The two independent LR-coefficient or interpolation implementations disagree, exceed their attested resource envelope, or verifier integrity cannot be established.
The separately approved experiment resource budget is exhausted.
